subject: Emotions
title: Emotional Agility
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Emotional Agility.

hook.text: Susan David was told 'just be positive' after her father died. She refused. Forced positivity isn't emotional health.

buildup.text: Emotional agility means holding emotions lightly—not suppressing, not wallowing, but stepping through them.

discovery.text: Rigid responses fail: always suppressing anger or always venting it. Agility means flexible response based on context.

twist.text: Toxic positivity is a form of emotional rigidity. Insisting on happiness makes people feel broken for feeling sad.

climax.text: The agile approach: acknowledge the feeling, notice its message, choose your action based on values, not impulse.

punchline.text: Emotional health isn't feeling good. It's feeling accurately.

quiz.question: What does Susan David argue against?
